This page declares the Wave 3 preparation targets tangled by `_targets.R`.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Approve The Curation Contract"}

The source-inspection page must first record the source schema, record grain,
stable keys, pre-/post-DHIS2 boundary, missing-value semantics, validation
rules, and disclosure controls.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Declare The Parquet Transformation Boundary"}

Declare the shared file-to-file transformation used by this page and by the
clinic-month inventory. Each caller supplies its dependencies and output path.

The helper below opens Parquet inputs with automatic materialization into R
disabled, applies the supplied transformation, and writes the result through
DuckDB. Only the output path crosses the target boundary. Input paths, output
paths, and transformation dependencies stay explicit at each call site.

```{r}
s0_pipeline_parquet_transform_fn <- function(
  input_paths, output_path, transform, read_options = list()
) {
  input_paths <- unname(as.character(input_paths))
  stopifnot(
    length(input_paths) > 0L,
    all(file.exists(input_paths)),
    length(output_path) == 1L, !is.na(output_path), nzchar(output_path),
    is.function(transform)
  )

  relation <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(
    input_paths,
    prudence = "stingy",
    options = read_options
  )
  result <- transform(relation)

  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  duckplyr::compute_parquet(result, output_path)
  output_path
}
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Read One Raw RMA File With Explicit Types"}

In this first section of the script, we take raw files and prepare them
by aggregating them into a tracked Parquet file, one row per
clinic-year-month, and one column per health outcome-age-sex.

Applies only to 2020-2022 data.

We've also opted-in to using DuckDB via the `duckplyr` package
to avoid in-memory limitations.

```{r}
library(targets)
library(readr)
library(openxlsx)
library(duckplyr)
library(cli)

tar_load(s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr)
```


We have a variable number of missing values in our
first rows of data, so we'll need to ensure they don't
get read as logical NAs. The `duckplyr` `options`
list allows us to force `DOUBLE` and `VARCHAR` types: 

The archived CSVs also use literal `NA` for missing values. The legacy
`readr::read_csv()` reader recognizes both empty fields and `NA` as missing;
set DuckDB's `nullstr` explicitly to preserve that rule before converting
measurements to `DOUBLE`. Otherwise row-count diagnostics can succeed while
the Parquet write fails when it evaluates the measurement columns. Missing
values remain null, including in entirely missing numeric columns.


```{r}
s0_clinic_RMA_read_nonlogical_fn <- function(filepath){

  readr_spec <- spec_csv(filepath) 
  spec_names <- names(readr_spec$cols)

  readr_spec %>%
    as.character() %>%
    str_split_1("") %>%
    tibble(spec = .) %>%
    mutate(
      name = spec_names,
      duckdb_dtype = case_when(
        str_detect(name, regex("description", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "VARCHAR",
        spec == "c" ~ "VARCHAR",
        spec == "d" ~ "DOUBLE",
        spec == "l" ~ "DOUBLE",
        .default = "DOUBLE"
      )
    ) %>%
    select(name, duckdb_dtype) %>%
    deframe() -> duckdb_spec

  
  # Set the CSV dialect explicitly. Auto-detection samples only the first
  # rows, so a quoted comma appearing later can otherwise be misclassified as
  # an extra column.
  read_csv_duckdb(
    filepath,
    options = list(
      types = list(duckdb_spec),
      nullstr = list(c("", "NA")),
      delim = ",",
      quote = "\"",
      escape = "\""
    )
  ) %>%
    return()
  
}

```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Declare The Clinic-Month Maximum Reduction"}

Define the reducer shared by the per-file and cross-file aggregation stages.
Missing grouping keys fail before a result can be written.

The reductions below use operations that `duckplyr` translates to DuckDB.
DuckDB's `MAX()` ignores null values and returns null for an all-null group,
which preserves the behavior of the previous `max_or_na()` helper without
materializing columns in R.

```{r}
s0_clinic_RMA_summarise_group_max_fn <- function(df) {
  grouping_columns <- c("organisationunitid", "periodname")
  missing_grouping_columns <- setdiff(grouping_columns, names(df))
  if (length(missing_grouping_columns)) {
    stop(
      "Cannot calculate clinic-month maxima; missing grouping column(s): ",
      paste(missing_grouping_columns, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  df |>
    summarise(
      across(
        -all_of(grouping_columns),
        ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .by = all_of(grouping_columns)
    )
}

```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Write One Reduced Parquet Branch"}

Read one source file, remove redundant columns, compute its clinic-month
maxima, and write the branch artifact. The small row-count diagnostics are
collected for the execution log; the measurement table stays in DuckDB.

```{r}
s0_clinic_RMA_process_csv_fn <- function(csv_path, output_path=here("data/intermediates"), drop_cols = c("organisationunitcode", "organisationunitdescription")) {
  stopifnot(length(csv_path) == 1L, file.exists(csv_path))
  
  cli_alert_info(paste("Working on:", csv_path))
  
  # Read file with type-safe reader
  temp_df <- s0_clinic_RMA_read_nonlogical_fn(csv_path)
  
  # Drop the extra columns if they exist
  temp_df <- temp_df %>%
    select(-any_of(drop_cols))
  
  # Calculate diagnostics in DuckDB and collect only the two scalar results.
  file_stats <- temp_df |>
    summarise(
      group_rows = n(),
      .by = c(organisationunitid, periodname)
    ) |>
    summarise(
      rows = sum(group_rows),
      duplicate_rows = sum(group_rows - 1L)
    ) |>
    collect()

  cli_alert_info(paste(
    "Successfully created dataframe for", csv_path, "with shape",
    file_stats$rows[[1]], "x", length(names(temp_df))
  ))
  cli_alert_info(paste(
    "Number of duplicate clinic-month-year records:",
    file_stats$duplicate_rows[[1]]
  ))
  
  # Description fields are assigned VARCHAR when the CSV relation is created.
  result = s0_clinic_RMA_summarise_group_max_fn(temp_df)
  
  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  compute_parquet(result, output_path)

  output_path
}
```

`s0_clinic_RMA_process_csv_fn()` intentionally accepts exactly one path, and never holds other input tables in
memory. `_targets.R` selects the `RMA_W3_FULL` paths in
`s0_clinic_RMA_W3_raw_paths_chr`, then declares one file-tracking branch per
path in `s0_clinic_RMA_W3_raw_csv`. The Parquet writer maps over those tracked
file branches outside this notebook. That makes each CSV
independently schedulable and means the branch artifacts contain parquet files
rather than raw csvs. Dynamic branching enables parallel execution;
the approved Slurm allocation and selected `targets` backend determine how
many branches run concurrently.

The second reduction in `_targets.R` combines the smaller branch summaries and
takes the clinic-month maximum again. This is equivalent to taking the maximum
over the fully combined raw data because maximum is associative:

\[
\max(\text{all rows}) = \max(\max(\text{file 1}), \ldots, \max(\text{file N}))
\]

This two-stage reduction was introduced after the raw-table aggregation was
OOM-killed with a 120 GiB Slurm allocation. It is a memory-scaling change, not
a change to the numeric maximum rule. The current reducer retains the prior
rule for every non-grouping field; a later curation decision should define
field-specific behavior for names, descriptions, and codes rather than treating
a lexicographic character maximum as scientific metadata.

::: {.callout-warning title="Why aggregation stays in DuckDB"}

The per-file reductions completed, but the final target was OOM-killed in a
120 GiB Slurm allocation. The diagnostic evidence is that files can have zero
duplicate clinic-month keys. In that situation, a per-file group maximum has
nearly the same cardinality as the input, so the previous R-based final target
needed to materialize all branch summaries at once. Increasing the requested memory is
not the next proposed experiment.

The per-file target now implements a disk-backed DuckDB/duckplyr boundary. Its
stages are:

1. preserve the existing one-file CSV reading, UTF-8, and type-normalization
   behavior;
2. execute each per-file clinic-month `MAX` reduction in DuckDB;
3. write each branch result to Parquet without materializing it in R.

The final target below reads all branch Parquet paths as one DuckDB relation,
executes the final clinic-month reduction, and persists that result through
another file target.

The aim is to preserve the original code's transformation logic as closely as
possible. The change is the execution engine and storage boundary, not a
redesign of the data-cleaning rules. Before implementation, the output schema
and reducer for metadata fields must be made explicit: numeric measures use
maximum, whereas names, descriptions, and codes require a domain-specific
rule. DuckDB and duckplyr are declared runtime dependencies.

:::

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Combine The Reduced Branches"}

Apply the same reduction to the branch files to obtain one tracked group-maximum
artifact. No raw measurement table needs to be collected into R.

Calculate the group maxima across all branch artifacts with the shared helper.
`union_by_name` preserves columns that occur in only some source files.

```{r}
#| format: file
s0_clinic_RMA_W3_group_max_parquet <- s0_pipeline_parquet_transform_fn(
  input_paths = s0_clinic_RMA_W3_within_file_max_parquet,
  output_path = here("data/intermediates/RMA_W3_group_max.parquet"),
  transform = s0_clinic_RMA_summarise_group_max_fn,
  read_options = list(union_by_name = TRUE)
)
```

:::

:::{.manual-procedure title="Crosswalk with GESIS Data"}

Our next step is to crosswalk the clinic data with GESIS DHIS data to get the
exact questions for each measure.

```{r}
#| format: file
s0_gesis_xwalk_raw_csv <- s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr |>
  str_subset("mapping DHIS2 GESIS 2010 2022")
```

```{r}
s0_gesis_xwalk_nonmissing_uid_df <- read_csv(s0_gesis_xwalk_raw_csv) |>
  select(UID...12, code_fs, TYPE, FS) |>
  rename(organisationunitid = UID...12) |> #correct the naming of organisationunitid
  distinct() |>                            #tidy up missingness
  filter(!is.na(organisationunitid))
```

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Write The Cleaned Wave 3 Table"}

Use the descriptive crosswalk and the reviewed period-specific substitutions
to produce the cleaned Parquet artifact.

Lastly, we `left_join` the RMA wave 3 data with this crosswalk on Organisation.
The last bit of cleaning correctly maps diagnoses that changed names slightly between wave 3 subwaves

```{r}
#| format: file
s0_clinic_RMA_W3_clean_parquet <- s0_pipeline_parquet_transform_fn(
  input_paths = s0_clinic_RMA_W3_group_max_parquet,
  output_path = here("data/intermediates/clinic_RMA_W3_clean.parquet"),
  transform = function(relation) {
    relation |>
      left_join(as_duckdb_tibble(s0_gesis_xwalk_nonmissing_uid_df), by = "organisationunitid") |>
      mutate(
        # rows of AME where periodcode > 202300 should be values of AME prem;
        `T13: AME 0-6 mois` = if_else(
          periodcode > 202300,  `T13: AME premiere heure 0-6 mois`, `T13: AME 0-6 mois`
        ),
        # etc
        `T13: AME 1ère heure` = if_else(
          periodcode > 202300, `T13: AME premiere heure 1ère heure`, `T13: AME 1ère heure`
        ),
        `MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)` = if_else(
          periodcode > 202300, `CHU CHRR T26 MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)`, `MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)`
        )
      ) |>
      # remove redundant
      select(
        -any_of(c(
          "T13: AME premiere heure 0-6 mois",
          "T13: AME premiere heure 1ère heure",
          "CHU CHRR T26 MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)"
        ))
      ) |>
      mutate(V1 = row_number() - 1L) |>
      select(V1, everything())
  }
)
```
:::

Important: there is a chance that the assignment of V1 to row number doesn't
work here, due to the fact that the data is now in a Parquet and row numbers
are only computed at evaluation time.

absent from this ZIP; a prior inspection established that the generic member
has the same bytes. No Drive file is read. Extract only this member into the

Load the pair for this page. Braces keep these session assignments out of

```{r}
{
  archived_baseline <- dget(here::here("src", "archived-comparison-baseline.R"))
  legacy_path <- utils::unzip(
    here::here(archived_baseline$archive_zip), files = archived_baseline$wave3_archive_member,
    exdir = tempdir()
  )
  old_w3 <- duckplyr::read_csv_duckdb(

```

**Rows and columns.**

Collect only the row-count summaries. Use `length(names(...))` for column
counts: `ncol()` requests dimensions and triggers materialization of the
original relation, which `prudence = "stingy"` disables. Collecting a summary
does not materialize or replace `old_w3` or `new_w3`.

```{r}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = old_w3 |> dplyr::summarise(rows = dplyr::n()) |>
    dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::mutate(columns = length(names(old_w3))),
  `current pipeline` = new_w3 |> dplyr::summarise(rows = dplyr::n()) |>
    dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::mutate(columns = length(names(new_w3))),
  .id = "source"
)
```

**Column names and order.**

```{r}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = tibble::tibble(position = seq_along(names(old_w3)), column = names(old_w3)),
  `current pipeline` = tibble::tibble(position = seq_along(names(new_w3)), column = names(new_w3)),
  .id = "source"
)
```

**Reporting-period row counts. Period keys are displayed as integers on both sides.**

```{r}
# Shape check: w3-periods
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = old_w3 |> dplyr::count(periodcode, name = "rows") |>
    dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::mutate(periodcode = as.integer(periodcode)),
  `current pipeline` = new_w3 |> dplyr::count(periodcode, name = "rows") |>
    dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::mutate(periodcode = as.integer(periodcode)),
  .id = "source"
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = rows, values_fill = 0L) |>
  dplyr::mutate(difference = `current pipeline` - `most recent archived data`) |>
  dplyr::arrange(periodcode) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

An absent period contributes zero rows; `difference` is current minus archived.

**Diagnose row coverage before comparing measurement values.**

Run the read-only diagnostic in an authorized analysis session. It compares
the most recent archived data with the current pipeline, inventories both raw
source trees, and checks that their distinct clinic-month keys survive into
their respective prepared outputs. It then compares the legacy `readr` key
reader with the stored DuckDB reader on the selected separate-year delivery,
verifies the crosswalk's content identity, and reconciles the final row-count
difference using the join multiplicities. It builds no targets and changes
no pipeline outputs. Keep its data-derived summaries outside rendered HTML.

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript scripts/diagnose-w3-row-coverage.R
```

The legacy script and current implementation differ at these boundaries:

| Boundary | Legacy script 0 | Current DuckDB pipeline | Diagnostic implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Raw file selection | Recursively lists `.csv` files below its local `RMA_W3_FULL` directory. | Selects staged inventory paths containing `RMA_W3_FULL`; tracks and processes each file separately. | Compare actual selected paths and file versions before attributing differences to an engine. Separate-year and combined-year exports need not contain the same records. |
| CSV parsing | `readr::spec_csv()` with inferred logical collectors replaced by `col_number()`, followed by `readr::read_csv()`. | Uses the inferred specification to request `VARCHAR` or `DOUBLE`, forces description fields to `VARCHAR`, and sets CSV delimiter/quoting explicitly. | Types, missing-value interpretation, and character parsing require comparison. The diagnostic projects the grouping keys and tests both readers on identical files. |
| Maximum reduction | Combines all raw tables in R, then takes one `data.table` maximum per clinic ID and period name. Converts `-Inf` results to missing. | Takes per-file maxima, unions Parquet schemas by column name, then takes maxima again in DuckDB. All-null SQL maxima remain null. | Both use the same grouping key. Associativity preserves numeric maxima on identical parsed inputs; verify key conservation separately from value/type equivalence. |
| Facility crosswalk | Selects UID, code, type, and name; removes exact duplicates and missing UIDs; left-joins on UID. | Performs the same selection and join through DuckDB. | Several distinct crosswalk records may match one UID and expand a clinic-month into multiple rows. Compare multiplicity, not just distinct key counts. |
| Final corrections and storage | Uses indexed assignments for the period-specific diagnosis substitutions, adds a sequential `V1`, and writes CSV. | Uses `if_else()` for the same substitutions, adds `row_number() - 1`, and writes Parquet. | These operations do not deliberately filter rows. Row order and export indices are not stable alignment keys; types and missing-period behavior need separate value checks. |

The source decision is settled: reproduce the hand-delivered May 2025 ZIP.
Use its separate-year raw files for W3 preparation and its archived outputs
for comparison. The synced Drive delivery is excluded. Previously built
Drive-based targets require rebuilding before this comparison is meaningful.

:::
